tools.name: etf_profile

tools.name: etf_holdings
tools.description: What a fund holds, by weight, and how old the book is (lag_days: an issuer file read today and a filing from two months ago both come back). Use after etf_profile, or before etf_overlap.

tools.name: etf_theme
tools.description: Every US listed fund in a theme, largest first, with its fee and its share already in the S&P 500. For "what X ETFs are there" it returns the whole published set, not a sample.

tools.name: etf_themes
tools.description: Every theme ETFIQ publishes and how many funds each holds. Call when unsure what a theme is called, then etf_theme.

tools.name: etfiq_page
tools.description: Read any published ETFIQ page as text (theme hub, ranking, comparison, issuer, methodology note, dated study). Takes a path like /themes/cyber or a full etfiq.com URL. Reaches all 40,000 pages and returns content, not navigation.

tools.name: etfiq_sections
tools.description: What ETFIQ publishes, section by section with page counts, and start_here: the main pages (flows, weekly report, model portfolios, issuers, methodology, rankings, screener). Start here when the question is not about one fund.

tools.name: etfiq_list
tools.description: The pages inside one section, optionally only addresses containing a word. Use after etfiq_sections, then etfiq_page. count is the whole matching set even when the list is capped.

tools.name: etf_screen
tools.description: Every fund matching filters, with net assets and the source and date of that number. Filters: desk, issuer, max_fee_pct, min_assets_usd, tracks (index), min_yield_pct (12-month), pays (payout frequency), sort. count is the whole set: when fewer rows return, truncated and note say so; first names eve

tools.name: etf_overlap
tools.description: How much weight two funds hold in common, as published on their comparison page. Use to ask whether two ETFs are the same thing. Refuses rather than estimating when the pair is not compared or a holdings book is incomplete.

tools.name: etfiq_as_of
tools.description: What ETFIQ published on a given date, from its frozen dated archive. Use for a past date, or when a number must stay true after it is quoted: every other tool answers about today. Takes YYYY-MM-DD; covers the pieces written that night, not any per-fund number on any day.

tools.name: etf_holders
tools.description: Which US listed ETFs hold a company (a company, not a fund), ranked by weight, with the weight its issuer published and the book's date; bond funds holding its debt are listed separately. Answers "which ETFs hold X" and "which fund holds the most X". Takes a name or ticker. Covers 31,019 companies.

tools.name: etf_rankings
tools.description: The ranked lists ETFIQ publishes, or one of them. Each ranks one published number inside a stated set, such as the cheapest funds in a theme or buffer funds closest to their cap. No argument lists them.

tools.name: etf_flows
tools.description: Fund flows as ETFIQ computes them: daily change in shares outstanding times NAV. With ticker: that fund's net flow over 1D, 1W, 1M, 3M, YTD and 1Y with dates, share of starting net assets and streak. Without: the biggest inflows and outflows among funds with daily data for window (default 1W), funds

tools.name: find_page
tools.description: The designed ETFIQ pages that answer a question, best first, at most three (fund, comparison, holders of a company, ranking, theme, category, issuer, flows, screen, benchmark, FAQ, methodology). findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp.etfiq.com" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: etfiq_page · Private data: etf_holdings, build_portfolio, strategy_record · Public sink: etf_theme, etf_flows, list_benchmarks, compare_to_benchmark, etf_committee, etf_risk_check · Destructive: build_portfolio, etf_promise.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: etfiq_page · Private data: etf_holdings, build_portfolio, strategy_record · Public sink: etf_theme, etf_flows, list_benchmarks, compare_to_benchmark, etf_committee, etf_risk_check · Destructive: build_portfolio, etf_promise

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
